questions: Did these abnormal movements begin before you were 20 years old?
Have you had yellowing of the eyes or skin, dark urine, abdominal swelling, or other liver problems?
Has anyone in your family had similar movements or an unexplained liver or neurological disease?
Have you noticed difficulty speaking or swallowing?
Have you had a seizure or loss of consciousness?
Did the abnormal movements start in one limb and then spread to other limbs or the trunk?
Are the movements or abnormal postures worse when you try to walk, write, or perform another voluntary action?
Do the movements improve substantially after sleep?
Can a light touch to your face or another body part temporarily reduce the abnormal posture?
Have you ever taken levodopa or a similar Parkinson’s medicine, with clear improvement in the movements?
Were you born prematurely or did you have a lack of oxygen, severe jaundice, or another serious complication around birth?
Did you have delayed motor development or difficulty walking during childhood?
Have these movements steadily worsened over time rather than remaining stable?
Have you ever taken antipsychotic medicines, metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, or other medicines that can cause abnormal movements?
Do you have involuntary tongue movements, frequent biting of your tongue, or difficulty keeping your mouth closed?
Do you have involuntary twisting movements or abnormal postures involving your legs, trunk, or neck in addition to your arms?
Have you developed problems with balance or walking?
Have you had progressive forgetfulness, decline in school/work performance, or other cognitive changes?
Have you had depression, hallucinations, major personality changes, or other psychiatric symptoms?
Do your symptoms improve after sleep and become worse later in the day?
orders: Serum copper concentration and liver function tests
Brain MRI with T1-, T2-, and susceptibility-weighted sequences to exclude structural or neurodegenerative causes of generalized dystonia
Genetic testing for the TOR1A (DYT1) pathogenic variant, including deletion/duplication analysis
If TOR1A testing is negative, an isolated-dystonia gene panel including THAP1 (DYT6), KMT2B, and GNAL variants
